dossiers.title: The four entities, Foundation rights and the brand
dossiers.focus: Build a legal-entity and rights map before interpreting the company’s founding story, ownership or educational obligations.

definitions.definition: The listed holding company; distinguish it from the commercial operating company, the charity and the charity’s shareholding subsidiary.
definitions.locator: Companies House overview; compare annual report physical p127

definitions.definition: A defined relationship in the listing and contractual framework, not a synonym for owning more than half of all shares.
The prospectus describes a particular trademark-linked obligation with a price formula, qualifications and remedy process; it is not a blanket price ceiling on the entire product range.

readings.title: Start with the charity’s legal record
readings.section: Companies House overview and incorporation record
readings.what_to_read: Record the Foundation’s company number and incorporation date; separately identify its charity registration.
readings.why_this_reading: The public-facing founding date, company incorporation and charity registration describe different events.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A first node for the entity map, with date type explicitly labeled.

readings.title: Identify the commercial company
readings.section: Companies House overview and filing history: incorporation and name changes
readings.what_to_read: Read the incorporation and initial name-change records alongside the commercial company’s present legal name.
readings.why_this_reading: The prospectus history’s December 2012 incorporation wording needs to be reconciled with the registry record.
readings.evidence_to_capture: Exact company number, incorporation date, initial name and date of the change to Raspberry Pi (Trading).

readings.title: Identify the quoted holding company
readings.section: Companies House overview and initial 2024 filings
readings.what_to_read: Record the holding company’s incorporation, name changes and plc status.
readings.why_this_reading: A newly incorporated holding entity does not mean the commercial business began in 2024.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A third node; leave the shareholding subsidiary to Note 30.

readings.title: Read the relationship agreement rights
readings.what_to_read: Follow independence undertakings, related-party voting restrictions and the thresholds for nominating directors.
readings.why_this_reading: Share percentage, voting arrangements and nomination rights are different pieces of evidence.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A rights table with threshold, beneficiary, action permitted and termination condition.

readings.title: Read the brand assignment and licence
readings.what_to_read: Read the price formula and every condition between a breach and possible trademark reassignment.
readings.why_this_reading: A simplified “Foundation owns the brand” or “all Pis must stay below $45” description would miss the contractual structure.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A flowchart of ownership, licence back, product obligation and remedy sequence.

readings.title: Bring the ownership and related-party record forward
readings.what_to_read: Compare the year-end shareholder table, concert-party wording, recharge arrangements and trademark account with the prospectus.
readings.why_this_reading: The annual report gives a later snapshot but contains date/registration wording that needs careful entity attribution.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A dated shareholding map; a discrepancy log for the trademark date and the Mid Co registration number.

readings.title: Read the Foundation’s own explanation
readings.section: IPO and the Foundation’s future funding
readings.what_to_read: Read what the charity says the IPO proceeds allow it to do and how it describes the commercial relationship.
readings.why_this_reading: This is the counterparty’s primary account, with a different organizational purpose.
readings.evidence_to_capture: Separate charity proceeds and charitable spending from cash raised or spent by the listed group.

readings.title: Read the Foundation’s April 2026 secondary placing
readings.section: Results of offering: seller, proceeds, strategic investor, remaining holding and expected settlement
readings.what_to_read: Read the final announced sale terms and distinguish the Foundation’s proceeds from the listed company’s cash. Mark the settlement date as expected in this release.
readings.why_this_reading: The annual report’s year-end ownership snapshot predates this transaction announcement.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A transaction row showing announcing party, seller, shares, intended buyer participation, remaining holding and settlement status.

readings.title: Replace the year-end snapshot with dated TR-1 evidence
readings.section: TR-1 sections 1–9; read together with the linked Foundation, Arm and SW filings
readings.what_to_read: Read the latest Ezrah filing and the linked holder filings. Preserve each threshold-crossing, issuer-notification and publication date; retain the section 1 versus 8A identifier discrepancy for clarification.
readings.why_this_reading: A placing announcement and a filed resulting holding are different evidence. A later filing for one holder is not a current register for every holder.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A holder-by-holder ledger with voting rights, denominator/date basis, direct/indirect chain, source identifier and unresolved discrepancies.

related_sources.title: Foundation holding after the April transaction — 29 April 2026
related_sources.section: TR-1 sections 1–9; compare threshold date, publication date and identifiers

related_sources.title: Arm holding after the April transaction — 28 April 2026
related_sources.section: TR-1 sections 1–9; compare threshold date, publication date and identifiers

related_sources.title: SW Investment Management latest notification — 19 August 2026
related_sources.section: TR-1 sections 1–9; compare threshold date, publication date and identifiers

questions: Which legal entity owns each asset, employs the commercial team and holds the quoted shares?
Which dates describe incorporation, trading history, charitable registration and the 2024 group reorganization?
How do the Foundation and Ezrah holdings interact with the relationship agreements at each dated snapshot?
Which rights change at the stated ownership thresholds, and which rights attach to the trademark licence instead?
Exactly which product obligation is described, and how are manufacturing cost, taxes, shipping and remedies treated?
Can the September 2020 wording in the annual report, August 2021 narrative and September 2021 contract date be reconciled from filed documents?
Which Foundation-related cash movements are share sales, donations, recharges or ordinary commercial transactions?
What do the post-placing TR-1s and latest August notifications actually establish for each holder, and which date, denominator or identifier differences still need reconciliation?
evidence_required: A four-entity diagram with company numbers and dated ownership arrows.
A rights matrix supported by paragraph/page references.
An unresolved-date ledger that preserves conflicting original wording.
A dated TR-1 ledger; do not treat a transaction announcement or a single holder’s later filing as the current complete share register.

public: Registry incorporation/name-change records; prospectus agreements; annual related-party and shareholder notes; Foundation reporting.
The April placing and four selected April/August TR-1s are now hosted as reading copies; use them before seeking a terminal refresh.
terminal: Refresh the latest disclosed ownership and voting-rights announcements; retain the filing date for every holding.
human: Ask the company secretary or IR for the public document that reconciles the trademark date and entity-number wording.
Ask the Foundation about its published governance and funding arrangements, rather than commercial sales information.

dossiers.completion_test: In your own words, explain how the charity can influence the listed company without treating all four entities as one organization. Point to the clause behind each right and state which date discrepancy remains unresolved.
dossiers.locator_convention: Physical PDF page numbers are one-based viewer pages, not printed page labels. Web readings use named sections.

dossiers.title: What is actually inside a Raspberry Pi product?
dossiers.focus: Learn the board, module and chip boundaries well enough to inspect a product, read a customer design and identify whose technology performs each function.

definitions.definition: A single-board computer exposes usable connectors; a compute module packages the core computing functions for integration with a carrier and other system components.
Raspberry Pi’s peripheral controller used alongside the main application processor in Pi 5; it is not a replacement name for Broadcom BCM2712.
RP2040/RP2350 belongs to a separate device category from the Linux application processor in a Pi board.

readings.title: Establish the product taxonomy
readings.section: Business overview; hardware and semiconductor IP
readings.what_to_read: Separate SBCs, compute modules, accessories and semiconductor products. Identify the named collaborators and owned IP blocks.
readings.why_this_reading: Revenue labels become easier to interpret when the physical objects are clear.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A one-page product tree with a photograph or schematic reference for each category.

readings.title: Read Pi 5’s actual specification
readings.what_to_read: Locate the application processor, RP1 role, memory options, external interfaces, power requirement and temperature range.
readings.why_this_reading: Marketing performance statements and physical design requirements answer different questions.
readings.evidence_to_capture: An annotated board diagram; mark specifications as belonging to this document revision.

readings.title: Follow the Pi 5 I/O split
readings.what_to_read: Trace the PCIe connection and the functions on the two sides of it; read what the internal RP1 processor does.
readings.why_this_reading: This prevents the phrase “own silicon” from collapsing several distinct engineering roles.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A two-chip diagram showing CPU, peripheral interfaces and connection between chips.

readings.title: Translate an SBC into a module design
readings.what_to_read: Read what CM5 includes, what Lite omits and what a carrier must provide. Include antenna/certification and supported PCIe qualifications.
readings.why_this_reading: A bare module is only one component in an OEM product.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A module-versus-carrier responsibility list with three concrete interfaces.

readings.title: Separate the MCU software world
readings.what_to_read: Read the microcontroller use cases, Pico software stack and relationship to other embedded operating systems.
readings.why_this_reading: A Pico, RP2350 chip and Pi 5 should not be treated as interchangeable products.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A second block diagram for an MCU application; label the software environment.

readings.title: Hear the RP1 engineering explanation
readings.what_to_read: Read or listen for why the team separated peripheral functions and how that architecture was developed.
readings.why_this_reading: The engineers supply design context behind the short product brief.
readings.evidence_to_capture: Three design choices with the engineer’s stated reason and a transcript locator.

readings.title: Update the architecture and operating boundary
readings.what_to_read: Compare the current full-stack diagram with the IPO-era diagram and manufacturing boundary.
readings.why_this_reading: This distinguishes what changed in the reporting period from an old description being repeated.
readings.evidence_to_capture: An owned/licensed/collaboratively developed/manufactured-by-others matrix.

questions: Which chip runs Linux on Pi 5, and which chip handles the principal peripheral interfaces?
Which pieces of IP are described as Raspberry Pi-owned, licensed or collaboratively developed?
What must an OEM add to a CM5 before it can sell a finished product?
Which interface claims depend on drivers, a carrier board, adapters or certification conditions?
What work belongs on an MCU rather than a Linux board, and what evidence would establish that for a particular application?
How would you distinguish a hardware capability from a supported, tested product configuration?
Which advertised characteristics changed between document revisions, and which are still only product-page claims?
evidence_required: Two annotated architecture diagrams: Pi 5/CM5 and an RP2350-based application.
A component-responsibility matrix with source locators.
A product vocabulary sheet written without promotional adjectives.

public: Product briefs, datasheets, architecture interviews and report diagrams.
terminal: Use terminal product/segment labels only after translating them to the company’s disclosed product categories; no terminal is needed for circuit architecture.
human: Ask an embedded engineer to check the diagrams and identify anything a first-time integrator has omitted.
At a maker or engineering lab, inspect an SBC, compute module, carrier and MCU board side by side.

dossiers.completion_test: Explain a CM5-based finished product to another analyst using a blank sheet: identify the application processor, peripheral controller, memory, carrier, software and supplier for each element. Do not rely on “Raspberry Pi makes the whole computer” as the explanation.
dossiers.locator_convention: Physical PDF page numbers are one-based viewer pages, not printed page labels. Web readings use named sections.

dossiers.title: Why a board sale and a royalty look different in the accounts
dossiers.focus: Reconstruct the commercial and accounting routes before comparing revenue, units, gross profit or reported ASP.

definitions.definition: The group procures or manufactures products and sells them through resellers or directly to OEMs; the report distinguishes this from licence royalties.
The KPI is a weighted manufacturer-recommended retail price for boards sold during the period, rather than group revenue divided by board units.
A defined board metric whose scope includes royalties; use the company’s numerator and denominator rather than an improvised revenue margin.

readings.title: Read both routes together
readings.what_to_read: Follow title, stock ownership, customer contact, royalty flow and working-capital responsibility in each route.
readings.why_this_reading: The same physical product can generate very different reported revenue depending on its route.
readings.evidence_to_capture: Two flow diagrams with goods, cash and reported revenue separately drawn.

readings.title: Trace Farnell’s two roles
readings.what_to_read: Read the Approved Reseller route and Farnell’s licence operation, including its purchases as an Approved Reseller.
readings.why_this_reading: A counterparty name alone does not identify whether the transaction is royalty or direct revenue.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A Farnell role table: licensee, reseller, customer-support responsibility and reporting cadence.

readings.title: Read the actual licence summary
readings.what_to_read: Read the products covered, commercial responsibilities, territorial exception and written-extension condition.
readings.why_this_reading: The contractual end date is a dated disclosure, not evidence that an extension has or has not since been signed.
readings.evidence_to_capture: Contract terms as of IPO, plus a separately dated renewal-check field.

readings.title: Update the commercial model
readings.what_to_read: Read the current diagrams, product/channel revenue table and gross-profit discussion together.
readings.why_this_reading: The report supplies the later product mix and explains why channel comparisons require consistent boundaries.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A reported-only bridge between product units, channel revenue and royalty revenue.

readings.title: Read recognition rather than infer it
readings.what_to_read: Identify control transfer for product sales, royalty timing, returns/warranties and component repurchase accounting.
readings.why_this_reading: An operational shipment, royalty report and accounting recognition point need not be the same event.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A recognition-trigger table with one row per revenue or financing route.

readings.title: Read every KPI definition
readings.what_to_read: Read the definitions of board units, ASP, board gross profit, accessory gross profit and headcount.
readings.why_this_reading: This is the control page for any later spreadsheet calculations.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A unit/denominator dictionary; flag metrics that cannot be calculated from public revenue totals alone.

readings.title: Locate segment and geography boundaries
readings.what_to_read: Read the single-segment statement, geographic basis and major-customer disclosure.
readings.why_this_reading: Financial reporting categories should not be mistaken for management’s end-user market taxonomy.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A map from reported accounting categories to operating categories, with unmappable cells left blank.

questions: For each channel, who buys components, owns inventory, invoices the next buyer and handles first-line support?
At what point is each type of revenue recognized, and what document evidences that point?
When Farnell appears as a customer, can you tell which role it is performing?
Why might revenue per board differ from the disclosed ASP even when all arithmetic is correct?
Which metrics include accessory or royalty economics, and which exclude them?
Which parts of a channel-mix reconciliation are observable from filings and which remain undisclosed?
What public evidence establishes the licence status after the latest available disclosure?
evidence_required: Goods/cash/accounting flow diagrams for both routes.
A KPI dictionary reproducing scope and units in your own words.
A blank-cell reconciliation showing every unavailable split rather than estimating it.

public: Prospectus licence summary; annual recognition policy, revenue tables and KPI definitions; subsequent RNS.
terminal: Obtain full results-call Q&A and broker definition notes to see whether channel changes or licence renewal were discussed; distinguish analyst estimates from company disclosure.
human: Ask finance/IR for a public illustrative invoice-to-recognition example in each route.
Ask a distributor to explain its publicly discussable ordering and reporting process; do not request another customer’s transaction details.

dossiers.completion_test: Using a hypothetical identical board, explain how reported revenue differs across the two routes without inserting an assumed margin. Then explain why the published ASP is not a substitute for realized group revenue per unit.
dossiers.locator_convention: Physical PDF page numbers are one-based viewer pages, not printed page labels. Web readings use named sections.

dossiers.title: From an order to use in a customer’s product
dossiers.focus: Make the shipment, distributor stock, OEM purchase and installed-device observations distinct before interpreting demand language.

definitions.definition: Working research labels: sell-in records a supplier’s shipment into a channel; sell-through records onward sales at a specified channel stage. Define the stage each time.
A customer’s selection or engineering project is a different event from a production order or shipment; the report separately describes project discussions and sales.
The annual report describes supplying from inventory and a relatively small order book, which limits the forward-demand information in that book.

readings.title: Draw the order and reporting chain
readings.what_to_read: Follow credit terms, reseller reporting, licence reports and the definitions of direct and indirect OEM customers.
readings.why_this_reading: The observer’s position in the chain determines what its number can measure.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A chain with order date, shipment date, report date and end-use observation as separate fields.

readings.title: Read the shortage-era allocation account
readings.what_to_read: Read the April 2022 explanation of demand and product availability.
readings.why_this_reading: Historical allocation rules provide context for customer behavior during constrained supply.
readings.evidence_to_capture: The company’s dated statements on constraints and prioritization; no reconstructed missing demand.

readings.title: Read the recovery forecast as a forecast
readings.section: Supply-chain update and expected recovery through 2023
readings.what_to_read: Separate observed availability from the forward milestones in the December 2022 post.
readings.why_this_reading: A forecast should be tested against later observations, not entered as an achieved timeline event.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A forecast-versus-subsequent-evidence table with the original dates.

readings.title: Read the inventory-normalization account
readings.section: Financial review: channel normalization and working capital
readings.what_to_read: Separate management’s channel inventory description from stock actually recorded on the group balance sheet.
readings.why_this_reading: Channel inventory and company inventory belong to different owners and different data sets.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A two-owner inventory ledger and the source behind each balance or directional claim.

readings.title: Read the visibility limitation
readings.section: Principal risks: supply chain and demand forecasting
readings.what_to_read: Read how inventory commitments and short demand visibility coexist in the company’s account.
readings.why_this_reading: The report itself sets limits on how much a short order book can tell you.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A list of leading, contemporaneous and lagging observations, with their lag defined by the process.

readings.title: Read the latest dated operating update
readings.section: 5 June 2026 trading update, including outlook and footnotes
readings.what_to_read: Mark every actual, expected, minimum and consensus-reference statement separately.
readings.why_this_reading: A trading update contains both observations and forecasts, with different evidence status.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A disclosure table: statement, period, actual/forecast, source date and comparison basis.

readings.title: Separate commercial activity from conversion
readings.what_to_read: Read how opportunities enter the Board-to-Board and reseller processes.
readings.why_this_reading: Meetings, project discussions, prototypes and volume purchases require different evidence.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A customer-stage ladder with the document needed to move from each stage to the next.

questions: Whose shipment or inventory balance does each observed data point describe?
Can a reseller’s availability page distinguish customer demand from replenishment or a stock transfer?
What dates would connect a group shipment to a distributor sale and then an OEM installation?
How did allocation during the shortage affect the comparability of customer anecdotes across periods?
What evidence supports a claim that channel inventory normalized, and what part is a company statement rather than a measured balance?
Which reported customer-stage counts are conversations, evaluations, design selections or production orders?
How would you reconcile a channel interview that conflicts with management’s description without assuming either observation represents the whole business?
evidence_required: A dated channel-stage map.
An inventory owner/source matrix.
A repeatable observation sheet with exact SKU, location, stock status, price basis and date.

public: Historic supply posts, annual operating narrative, RNS and dated public reseller listings.
All 82 announcements in the issuer-linked feed retrieved on 5 September 2026 are saved, including every trading update in that feed; start with this archive.
terminal: Retrieve full results-call Q&A and broker channel surveys with sample size, date and respondent type preserved. The public announcement sequence is already saved in this pack.
human: Interview the same reseller role on repeated dates using the same SKU questions.
Ask an OEM buyer for a completed historical procurement cycle, distinguishing qualification, purchase and deployment.
Ask both high-volume and small buyers; document how you selected them.

dossiers.completion_test: Take one demand claim and state exactly which stage, owner and time window it describes. List the observations still required before translating it into a claim about final customer usage.

dossiers.title: Components, contract manufacturers and committed cash
dossiers.focus: Trace board and semiconductor supply separately, then connect the physical lead times to inventory ownership and purchase commitments.

definitions.definition: A contract electronics manufacturer assembles products for a customer; component sourcing and ownership can still sit with Raspberry Pi.
The prospectus describes external wafer fabrication and outsourced assembly/test steps for proprietary chips, distinct from board assembly.
A contracted future purchase obligation can exist without being an inventory asset or trade payable at the reporting date.

readings.title: Separate the two supply chains
readings.what_to_read: Read Sony board assembly, strategic components, IMEC/TSMC fabrication, outsourced packaging/test and the group’s own test operations.
readings.why_this_reading: A single “supplier” box hides different concentration, substitution and lead-time questions.
readings.evidence_to_capture: Two process maps, identifying the owner of materials at each step and the statement date.

readings.title: Read the historical contract terms
readings.what_to_read: Locate last-time-buy obligations, development commitments, non-cancellable orders and the stated price-adjustment provisions.
readings.why_this_reading: A supplier relationship description does not establish the customer’s contractual flexibility.
readings.evidence_to_capture: An IPO-date commitments table, explicitly marked historical.

readings.title: Update product cost and inventory context
readings.section: Financial review: gross profit, working capital and capital expenditure
readings.what_to_read: Read the processor-cost discussion, memory exposure, components versus finished products and the amended-supply reference.
readings.why_this_reading: This provides the report’s own bridge from physical supply decisions to cash and product economics.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A dated register of named changes, avoiding an extrapolation into undisclosed future unit costs.

readings.title: Read ownership and commitments in the notes
readings.what_to_read: Read component/finished-goods stock, provisions, CEM repurchase arrangements and the horizon of outstanding commitments.
readings.why_this_reading: Free-issued or repurchased components can be misclassified if one looks only at shipments.
readings.evidence_to_capture: An ownership and accounting table: inventory, financing liability, payable and executory commitment.

readings.title: Read the post-year-end amendment
readings.section: Note 32, Events after the reporting period
readings.what_to_read: Read the effective date, purchase period and amount alongside the supplier identification in the financial review.
readings.why_this_reading: This is later than the year-end commitment table and cannot simply be added without checking overlap and scope.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A pre-/post-amendment comparison with any unresolvable overlap left open.

readings.title: Read a memory-price change at product level
readings.what_to_read: Identify affected variants, effective price date and the company’s explanation of the memory market.
readings.why_this_reading: Variant-level actions are more precise than an undifferentiated “prices rose” statement.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A SKU/date/old-new-price source sheet, with taxes and channel basis specified.

readings.title: Read inventory coverage and funding language
readings.section: 5 June 2026 trading update: memory inventory and H2 outlook
readings.what_to_read: Separate owned low-density inventory, expected economics and possible use of debt facilities.
readings.why_this_reading: Coverage, future replenishment price and financing are different observations.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A source-dated list of what management said was already held, expected or under consideration.

readings.title: Compare the next product-price adjustment
readings.section: 1 April 2026 announcement: 3GB Pi 4 and price changes
readings.what_to_read: Read how a changed memory configuration and prices were communicated.
readings.why_this_reading: A changed SKU can alter comparability even if the product family name is unchanged.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A revision to the SKU sheet that preserves retired, added and continuing variants.

readings.title: Read the January 2026 inventory and memory baseline
readings.section: Year-end trading update: mitigation steps, memory coverage, H1/H2 visibility and consensus footnote
readings.what_to_read: Read the original January account of supplier qualification, lower-memory variants, inventory buffers and visibility. Compare each dated statement with the June update already assigned.
readings.why_this_reading: The January release provides the earlier public baseline; the later update should not be read back into what was known in January.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A January-to-June disclosure ledger that separates held inventory, expected demand coverage, mitigation actions and forward uncertainty.

questions: Who orders, owns, stores and finances components at each stage?
Which manufacturing steps depend on Sony, Broadcom, wafer fabrication, packaging/test or internal equipment?
Which stated alternatives are qualified capacity and which are plans or estimates?
How do purchase commitments differ from inventory, payables and financing arrangements in the accounts?
What scope and timing differences prevent simply adding the old and amended supply commitments?
Which memory generations and board variants are exposed to each dated price announcement?
What public evidence would establish whether a supplier substitution changes qualification work, lead time or software support?
Which claims about inventory coverage describe a period of protection rather than the cost of eventual replenishment?
Which memory and inventory statements were disclosed in January, what did June update, and which changes cannot be inferred from the public wording alone?
evidence_required: Separate board and chip supply maps with named companies and dated roles.
An inventory/commitment bridge with no double counting.
A versioned product-price and memory-configuration ledger.

public: Prospectus supplier contracts, annual inventory/commitment notes, product notices and trading updates.
terminal: Use Bloomberg/Capital IQ for dated component-industry research and supplier filings; retain memory type, contract/spot basis and forecast status. Do not substitute a generic DRAM index for Raspberry Pi’s purchase price.
human: Ask a contract-manufacturing or procurement practitioner to walk through a completed component-shortage response using a non-confidential example.
Ask IR which public disclosure updates the overlap between year-end commitments and the 2026 amendment.

dossiers.completion_test: Draw the path from a memory purchase commitment to an assembled board and then cash collection. Explain which balances appear before shipment, after shipment and only in the commitments note, using the company’s actual accounting language.

dossiers.title: How an industrial design reaches production
dossiers.focus: Follow a real embedded product from prototype through carrier design, qualification, factory programming and support. Identify what the customer still has to do.

definitions.definition: The board that connects a compute module to the power, interfaces and application-specific electronics required by a finished product.
The engineering and procurement steps by which a customer selects and incorporates a component; the sources describe prototypes, module use and custom products as distinct routes.
The prospectus describes compliance support and design partners, while making clear that normal testing and certification costs can still apply.

readings.title: Read the buy, module and custom-product choices
readings.what_to_read: Read the company’s explanation of moving from an SBC prototype to a module or custom design. Treat its volume crossover estimate as a contextual company estimate.
readings.why_this_reading: The relevant choice depends on the customer’s application and engineering resources.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A decision tree with variables to investigate, leaving each customer’s actual threshold blank.

readings.title: Read the integration requirements
readings.section: Wireless; PCIe; power sequencing; thermal behavior
readings.what_to_read: Identify the carrier, antenna, driver, shutdown and thermal requirements that affect product development.
readings.why_this_reading: A quick successful demo does not establish a production-ready design.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A qualification checklist tied to the exact CM5 revision and intended environment.

readings.title: Read the CM4-to-CM5 changes
readings.section: Appendix B: differences from Compute Module 4
readings.what_to_read: Read the pin, protection, USB and power differences.
readings.why_this_reading: Physical similarity needs to be tested against the actual migration notes.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A change-impact worksheet: circuit, software, test and certification tasks.

readings.title: Read who helps the OEM
readings.what_to_read: Read pre-compliance work, regional approvals, integrator assistance and the Approved Design Partner role.
readings.why_this_reading: Assistance does not automatically transfer responsibility for the customer’s finished product.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A responsibility matrix across Raspberry Pi, design partner, OEM, test house and manufacturer.

readings.title: Read the application engineers’ account
readings.section: Go-to-market; Roger Thornton and Ian Newton Q&A
readings.what_to_read: Read how inquiries become technical work and what the engineers mean by a proof of concept.
readings.why_this_reading: The report’s examples reveal process stages; their elapsed time is not a general qualification-cycle statistic.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A stage-by-stage interview guide with required evidence for moving to production.

readings.title: Inspect a finished industrial implementation
readings.what_to_read: Identify the functions and qualifications added around CM5; check the temperature and power conditions.
readings.why_this_reading: The finished product shows what lies beyond the module purchase.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A boundary diagram that separates module capabilities from KUNBUS’s added system design.

readings.title: Read the factory-programming example
readings.what_to_read: Read the manufacturing workflow the jig is intended to support, including configuration and production context.
readings.why_this_reading: Provisioning, test and traceability are activities between a working prototype and repeatable production.
readings.evidence_to_capture: Add a factory-programming stage to the process map without assuming that every OEM uses this jig.

questions: What is the customer’s finished product, workload, environment and expected service life?
Which parts of the design remain the OEM’s responsibility after it buys the module?
What must be demonstrated after a proof of concept before qualification and volume shipment?
Which CM4-to-CM5 changes would require work in the example you are studying?
What evidence would establish actual engineering hours, certification expense and elapsed time without relying on vendor estimates?
When would this customer prefer an SBC, a standard module, a turnkey custom product or an in-house design?
Who pays for sustaining engineering, component changes, factory programming and field failures?
Which stage causes projects to stop, and can you obtain a completed example of that outcome?
evidence_required: One end-to-end project map with stage owners and exit documents.
A carrier/module responsibility matrix.
A completed-product parts-and-functions map plus a list of evidence still needed from an engineer.

public: Datasheet migration appendix; public certification/support programs; finished-system documentation; application-engineering interview.
terminal: Collect published customer case studies and historical management Q&A about project duration or conversion; a terminal cannot supply a specific customer’s unpublished qualification record.
human: Ask an embedded product manager to narrate one completed project from requirements to production, using calendar milestones rather than a general satisfaction score.
Ask a design partner about a design that was revised or abandoned and what would have changed the choice.
At a lab, have an engineer inspect the carrier/module interface with you.

dossiers.completion_test: Explain why “the prototype worked” and “the customer is in production” require different evidence. Walk through one application and identify every party, deliverable and unresolved cost or timing question between those events.

dossiers.title: Software compatibility, updates and running a fleet
dossiers.focus: Separate the operating system, low-level hardware support, application code and fleet services. Design a small migration exercise that exposes the work a customer actually performs.

definitions.definition: The company describes layers including firmware, Linux support and higher-level system software; the hardware and software ownership boundaries are not identical.
The current OS documentation distinguishes routine package updates from moving to a new major operating-system release.
definitions.locator: Manage software and firmware updates; Upgrade to a new major version

definitions.definition: The Connect product page describes administration and updating of multiple devices; that capability does not by itself establish paid adoption or revenue.

readings.title: Start with the stack and maintenance model
readings.what_to_read: Read the three layers, testing approach, old-device support and separate microcontroller ecosystem.
readings.why_this_reading: Compatibility can refer to an instruction set, OS image, driver, peripheral or application; keep those separate.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A stack diagram with the party responsible for each layer.

readings.title: Read the current software product narrative
readings.what_to_read: Locate Connect, active-device observations and the relationship between new products and software work.
readings.why_this_reading: Device activity, product capability and software revenue are different measurements.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A statement ledger that distinguishes installed activity, launches and monetization disclosures.

readings.title: Read the actual maintenance instructions
readings.section: Editions; Architecture; Manage software and firmware updates; Upgrade to a new major version
readings.what_to_read: Compare routine updates, firmware choices and major-release migration.
readings.why_this_reading: This supplies a reproducible basis for a user-run migration test.
readings.evidence_to_capture: An update decision tree and a list of application/peripheral checks.

readings.title: Read what fleet service adds
readings.section: Fleet management; Organisation controls; Management API; Bulk provisioning
readings.what_to_read: Identify administration, update and provisioning functions; record the current commercial terms yourself.
readings.why_this_reading: A fleet service should be compared with the customer’s operating workflow.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A capability/requirement matrix; leave adoption and economics fields unfilled without evidence.

readings.title: Read an integrator’s software choices
readings.section: First boot and software setup; Recovery
readings.what_to_read: Compare the two documented software paths for Pi Vision and their setup responsibilities.
readings.why_this_reading: A real finished-product vendor can wrap the same computing module in different software experiences.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A role map for OS image, device management, application and recovery support.

readings.title: Read the hardware side of migration
readings.section: Boot diagnostics and EEPROM; Appendix B
readings.what_to_read: Follow boot support and hardware differences that a software-only migration plan might miss.
readings.why_this_reading: A successful application rebuild is only one part of replacing a module.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A combined hardware/software migration checklist.

readings.title: Read another module vendor’s software boundary
readings.what_to_read: Identify the vendor-supported software paths and recovery resources.
readings.why_this_reading: Comparison needs equivalent support scope and responsibilities.
readings.evidence_to_capture: The same support matrix completed for a second vendor, without ranking the options.

questions: What does “compatible” mean for the actual application: source, binary, peripheral, image or operational workflow?
Who maintains each software layer and who receives the support request when something fails?
What changes between a routine update and a major OS migration?
Which local modifications or drivers would make replacing the board require extra work?
What fleet tasks does the customer perform manually today, and which functions address them?
What evidence would distinguish free active devices from paying organizational deployments?
How would the customer recover from a failed update or replace a device in the field?
evidence_required: A stack/support ownership diagram.
A user-run migration log recording initial image, application, peripherals, time and failures.
A fleet requirements matrix and a separate commercial-evidence ledger.

public: OS maintenance instructions; Connect product documentation; integrator setup and recovery guides.
terminal: Search full transcripts and research for separately disclosed software revenue, paid endpoints or customer counts; keep “not disclosed” if none exists.
human: Ask an OEM maintainer to show a sanitized old-to-new release checklist and explain the work it required.
With your own test hardware, time setup, update, peripheral validation and recovery; have an engineer review the protocol first.

dossiers.completion_test: Describe one application migration in your own words, separating hardware replacement, OS changes, application changes and fleet operations. State which effort you personally observed and which remains an interview or disclosure gap.

dossiers.title: Production life, revisions and security responsibilities
dossiers.focus: Learn the distinction between continued production, software maintenance, component revision, product qualification and secure deployment.

definitions.definition: A stated minimum manufacturing availability for a named product; it is not the same as a warranty or a guarantee that every revision remains unchanged.
A hardware or component version can change while the product family name remains the same; compare revision histories and change notices.
The RP2350 whitepaper describes chip-level protections and the responsibilities left to the user’s application and deployment.

readings.title: Read the product-life promise exactly
readings.what_to_read: Read the production horizon, operating range and limitations around the finished configuration.
readings.why_this_reading: Availability, reliability metrics and warranty terms cannot be used interchangeably.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A commitments table with product, version, promise, qualifications and document date.

readings.title: Read module reliability and migration qualifications
readings.section: Wireless certification; thermal behavior; Appendix B
readings.what_to_read: Separate module conditions, system design requirements and migration changes.
readings.why_this_reading: An OEM must establish its own product’s operating conditions.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A list of evidence the finished-product qualification must supply.

readings.title: Read the threat-model boundary
readings.section: Introduction; security challenge context; security features
readings.what_to_read: Read what is optional, the silicon-revision context and the scope of the security features.
readings.why_this_reading: RP2350 security properties must not be generalized to every Raspberry Pi product.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A scope table: chip revision, feature, intended protection and stated limitation.

readings.title: Read the deployment responsibilities
readings.section: Application security and securing a product
readings.what_to_read: Read key management, software updates and deployment considerations conceptually; do not change irreversible device settings as part of this reading.
readings.why_this_reading: The chip’s protections depend on how a finished product is configured and maintained.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A responsibility checklist for the product team, with a question beside each item.

readings.title: Read the public revision-and-remediation record
readings.what_to_read: Read the company’s account of the challenge, affected silicon and response.
readings.why_this_reading: Security claims have a dated test and revision history.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A chronology of claim, tested revision, reported issue and stated response.

readings.title: Read a comparator’s lifecycle policy
readings.section: Module availability; carrier-board and software qualifications
readings.what_to_read: Identify which commitments attach to modules and which do not extend to evaluation hardware.
readings.why_this_reading: A comparison must use the same product boundary.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A side-by-side commitments table with exact part numbers still to verify.

readings.title: Inspect an actual component-change ledger
readings.section: Revision History: 8GB and 4GB variants, including Q2 2026
readings.what_to_read: Read the changes to memory, small components and pre-installed software across revisions.
readings.why_this_reading: Long product life can include managed changes.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A sample change-impact question set for an OEM qualification engineer.

questions: Which promise concerns manufacturing availability, and which concerns maintenance or warranty?
Does the customer qualify a family, a part number, a silicon revision or a complete hardware/software configuration?
What evidence is required after a component or module revision changes?
Which security properties are enabled by the chip and which depend on application configuration or operations?
What public evidence updates a security claim after the cited whitepaper’s date?
Who owns key management, update delivery, vulnerability response and replacement devices in the finished product?
How would a customer plan for a component end-of-life notice before its own installed fleet reaches end of service?
evidence_required: A product-life versus support versus warranty matrix.
A revision-aware security and qualification record.
A dated issue/remediation ledger with the limits of each source preserved.

public: Datasheets, revision histories, public security whitepaper and lifecycle policies.
terminal: Use company announcements and complete Q&A to locate public security or lifecycle updates; a market-data terminal cannot certify the customer’s deployment.
human: Ask an OEM quality engineer for its public or sanitized component-change approval process.
Ask a security maintainer how responsibilities are divided, using a generic completed product rather than undisclosed vulnerabilities.

dossiers.completion_test: Explain why a long production commitment and an enabled secure-boot feature answer different customer questions. Use one named product revision to identify the additional evidence needed for the finished system.
dossiers.locator_convention: Physical PDF page numbers are one-based viewer pages, not printed page labels. Web readings use named sections.

dossiers.title: Engineering work, development assets and amortization
dossiers.focus: Learn how engineering effort becomes an expense, a capitalized development asset, an amortization charge or a cash outflow. Keep the product-development narrative separate from accounting judgments.

definitions.definition: The report sets out criteria for recognizing qualifying development expenditure as an intangible asset; research and maintenance do not automatically qualify.
An accounting estimate of the period over which an asset is amortized; it is distinct from a product’s promised manufacturing lifetime.
The capital expenditure reconciliation includes costs reallocated into development assets that are not a new cash payment in that period.

readings.title: Read how the engineering team works
readings.what_to_read: Read concurrent product work, specialized teams, collaboration and testing.
readings.why_this_reading: The operating process supplies context for the categories later used in accounting.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A product-development process map, with possible research, development and maintenance stages.

readings.title: Read the current investment narrative
readings.what_to_read: Read product cadence, software work, engineering staffing and test investment.
readings.why_this_reading: Product announcements and accounting asset additions are related observations, not equivalent counts.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A dated engineering-activity ledger without estimates of unpublished project budgets.

readings.title: Read recognition and estimation policies
readings.section: Notes: development assets; critical judgments and estimates
readings.what_to_read: Read every capitalization criterion and the useful-life change.
readings.why_this_reading: This is the rule set needed to interpret the numbers.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A decision tree for expense versus capitalization; list the evidence behind each criterion.

readings.title: Read the intangible-asset roll-forward
readings.what_to_read: Follow additions, assets in development, transfers, amortization, useful lives and the impairment-testing descriptions.
readings.why_this_reading: Pipeline assets and on-market assets are at different stages.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A reported-figures roll-forward with each movement linked to a page.

readings.title: Reconcile cash expenditure and asset additions
readings.what_to_read: Read the cash/non-cash capital expenditure bridge and the development-cost/expense presentation.
readings.why_this_reading: Adding reported R&D expense and capital expenditure without reconciling reallocated amounts can double count work.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A cash/expense/asset-addition bridge that explicitly isolates non-cash entries.

readings.title: Read the reported versus adjusted bridge
readings.what_to_read: Follow the definitions and adjustments rather than assuming all development-related items are excluded from all metrics.
readings.why_this_reading: The same engineering activity can affect statutory and adjusted measures differently.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A metric treatment table for research, capitalized development, amortization and share-based compensation.

readings.title: Read the risks and the estimate sensitivity
readings.section: Principal risks; useful-life estimate; intangible assets
readings.what_to_read: Read failure/delay risk and the quantified effect of the useful-life change.
readings.why_this_reading: A management estimate needs its rationale, arithmetic effect and future review conditions kept distinct.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A question list on estimate support, without inventing an alternative asset valuation.

questions: Which engineering activities are research, qualifying development, maintenance or support under the company’s policy?
What evidence supports the point at which a project becomes eligible for capitalization?
How do cash expenditure, total asset additions and the income-statement charge reconcile?
Which movements are non-cash reallocations rather than additional money spent?
What changed in semiconductor useful lives, and what effect did the company report for that change?
How do accounting useful life, product-generation cadence and manufacturing-lifetime promises differ?
What publicly disclosed conditions triggered impairment review, and what conclusion and assumptions did the report state?
Which development-cost questions cannot be resolved without project-level data that the company does not publish?
evidence_required: A capitalization decision tree in your own words.
A reconciled cash/expense/intangible-asset movement worksheet.
A chronology of estimate changes and their disclosed effects.

public: Annual accounting policies, intangible notes, cash-capex bridge and APM reconciliation; prospectus engineering description.
terminal: Retrieve several years of broker models and transcript discussion to identify differing definitions of R&D and capex; preserve the original assumptions rather than blending them.
human: Ask finance/IR to walk through a published-category example of development cost from cash payment to amortization.
Ask an engineering manager about completed project gates and maintenance responsibilities, without requesting unreleased product plans.

dossiers.completion_test: Explain one pound or dollar of engineering effort through cash flow, expense and asset recognition using a hypothetical example that follows the published policy. Then reconcile the report’s actual totals without double counting non-cash additions.
dossiers.locator_convention: Physical PDF page numbers are one-based viewer pages, not printed page labels. Web readings use named sections.

dossiers.title: Customer evidence: a case study is a starting point
dossiers.focus: Build a customer evidence file that separates the customer’s product, its use of Raspberry Pi, commercial scale, decision process and the limits of public case studies.

definitions.definition: A named OEM product can establish that a technology is used in that application; it does not necessarily disclose units, contract duration or supplier revenue.
A customer’s total users or devices is a company-wide statistic unless the source explicitly attributes it to Raspberry Pi-based products.
Case studies and voluntary interviews are selected observations. Record the selection process before treating them as representative evidence.
definitions.locator: Physical pp16–17, 22; research protocol derived from the nature of these sources

readings.title: Establish the original customer categories
readings.what_to_read: Read the named OEM applications and the distinction between all active OEMs and direct customers.
readings.why_this_reading: A customer count needs its population and channel definition.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A customer roster with application, direct/indirect status if disclosed, date and source.

readings.title: Read a current case study with its boundaries
readings.what_to_read: Separate Sixfab’s overall scale, its product functions and the specific Raspberry Pi relationship described.
readings.why_this_reading: A customer’s installed devices cannot be assigned to the supplier without supporting attribution.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A claim table marked supplier-specific, customer-wide or not disclosed.

readings.title: Read an OEM’s own finished-product document
readings.what_to_read: Read the module, interfaces, enclosure/system features and qualifications.
readings.why_this_reading: The customer’s own document can corroborate product use and reveal what the customer contributes.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A corroborated application entry with an exact product/version.

readings.title: Follow the OEM’s operating documentation
readings.what_to_read: Locate the variant and maintenance features the customer offers to its users.
readings.why_this_reading: A shipped product’s operating obligations are more specific than an endorsement quote.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A question list for the product manager and for an end user of the same product.

readings.title: Read another application’s integration guide
readings.section: Hardware overview; power/thermal; first boot; recovery
readings.what_to_read: Identify the HMI product boundary and its documented software paths.
readings.why_this_reading: A second application lets you vary the workload while keeping the underlying module visible.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A second corroborated application entry; record any specification needing clarification.

readings.title: Read the company’s opportunity-stage language
readings.what_to_read: Separate named products, project discussions, proof-of-concept work and general examples.
readings.why_this_reading: The customer evidence file should not turn an early engagement into a production win.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A stage label and proof required for every prospective customer entry.

readings.title: Read a historical substitution example
readings.what_to_read: Read the account of an OEM’s component substitution during shortage conditions.
readings.why_this_reading: A time-specific decision is useful for interview design, but cannot establish the customer’s permanent preference.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A dated decision-context entry and the follow-up evidence required today.

readings.title: Read the original SECO partnership scope
readings.section: Strategic partnership with SECO: HMI, CM5, Connect/Clea and exploratory opportunities
readings.what_to_read: Separate the announced commercial agreement, proposed product integration and areas the partners say they will explore. Compare those statements with the later SECO product guide already assigned.
readings.why_this_reading: This establishes the dated starting commitments behind a later customer-product example. The footer labels it a non-regulatory RNS Reach release.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A promise-to-product chronology with each milestone’s own source; leave sales and production scale blank where not disclosed.

readings.title: Read the NComputing collaboration as a separate application
readings.section: Pi 500+ launch and LEAF OS collaboration; customer-scale and distribution-service notes
readings.what_to_read: Read the enterprise-endpoint software and operating model being offered. Keep NComputing’s company-wide customer/device totals separate from deployments of this new combination.
readings.why_this_reading: A partnership capability statement does not establish a specific paid deployment or its economics. Comparative benefits in this Reach release remain the partners’ claims.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A platform/responsibility diagram, a dated launch entry and a list of customer-origin evidence required to verify use.

questions: What exact customer product contains which Raspberry Pi component, and is that corroborated by the customer?
What does the customer’s public scale measure, and how much is explicitly attributed to Raspberry Pi?
Who chose the component, who qualified it, who buys it and who supports the final user?
What alternatives were evaluated for that specific design and requirement set?
Which customer examples were chosen by the company for publication, and which did you find independently?
Can you find a completed evaluation that selected something else, stopped, or later migrated away?
Would the same decision have been made outside the shortage, budget or engineering constraints of that period?
Which observations are repeatable across customer types and which remain a single case?

For SECO and NComputing, which statements concern an agreement, an available product, an exploratory opportunity or an observed customer deployment, and what public evidence advances each to the next stage?
evidence_required: A customer evidence ledger with exact product, source, stage and scale boundary.
At least one OEM-origin document for each application studied.
A sample-selection log and separate queues for adopted, rejected, stopped and replaced designs.

public: OEM manuals/datasheets, company case studies and public product announcements; these do not generally reveal supplier-specific revenue.
terminal: Find historical research interviews and customer references; preserve anonymization, sample size and whether the source independently verified adoption.
human: Ask product engineering, purchasing and field-service roles about the same completed design; compare their accounts.
Seek integrators who use several module vendors, and explicitly ask for examples where Raspberry Pi was not selected.
Ask permission to observe a finished product’s setup or maintenance; document what you actually see.

dossiers.completion_test: Present one customer in five minutes using only corroborated facts, then state exactly what the public record does not establish about scale, economics or persistence. Explain how your next interview would fill a specific missing cell.

dossiers.title: Compare alternatives for one job, not one specification
dossiers.focus: Prepare a comparison the analyst can perform for a specified workload. The reading set covers a Raspberry Pi board/module, an industrial module and a Jetson production-platform boundary; it does not rank them or claim to cover the whole market.

definitions.definition: The items being compared must provide the same required function: a chip, module, developer kit and finished industrial computer include different work and components.
definitions.locator: Physical pp80–81, 90; NVIDIA FAQ developer-kit section

definitions.definition: NVIDIA distinguishes production modules from evaluation kits in support, validation and intended use.
definitions.locator: Can Jetson developer kits be used as production systems?

definitions.definition: The Toradex datasheet explicitly directs readers to software resources to establish which hardware features are supported.
definitions.locator: Physical p5, Purpose of the datasheet

readings.title: Start with the company’s stated alternatives
readings.what_to_read: Read named alternatives and the company’s positioning, labeling comparative statements as management claims.
readings.why_this_reading: A competitor roster is a starting population, not a tested outcome.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A candidate list organized by workload and product boundary.

readings.title: Specify the Raspberry Pi SBC boundary
readings.what_to_read: Read the interfaces, memory, power, operating range and additions needed for the chosen workload.
readings.why_this_reading: The board price alone does not describe the whole working system.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A required-components list and qualification conditions.

readings.title: Specify the Raspberry Pi module boundary
readings.section: Core features; carrier interfaces; power; thermal
readings.what_to_read: Read only the interfaces and constraints needed by your chosen application.
readings.why_this_reading: The comparison must include the carrier and sustaining responsibilities.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A CM5 system configuration to test, including software and cooling.

readings.title: Read a current industrial-module alternative
readings.section: Revision history; introduction; memory and physical features
readings.what_to_read: Match the exact SKU to CPU/MCU, interfaces, memory, operating conditions and software qualifications.
readings.why_this_reading: A feature available on one SKU may be absent from another.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A same-workload configuration; mark every specification with its document revision.

readings.title: Check the current assembly revision
readings.what_to_read: Match the proposed module to its current assembly and software path.
readings.why_this_reading: A static datasheet does not replace a revision and support check.
readings.evidence_to_capture: An exact part/revision/software record.

readings.title: Establish the Jetson production boundary
readings.section: Developer kits versus production modules; Super Mode
readings.what_to_read: Read which carrier, software and thermal work is needed beyond evaluation.
readings.why_this_reading: A developer-kit demonstration is not an equivalent production configuration.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A list of production additions and the evidence needed for a workload test.

readings.title: Check the matching lifecycle promise
readings.section: Production module availability; PCN/EOL; developer-kit exclusions
readings.what_to_read: Record the promise for the exact module, with retrieval date.
readings.why_this_reading: Lifecycle comparisons require equivalent products and dates.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A lifecycle field on the same comparison sheet.

readings.title: Use a finished product as a boundary check
readings.what_to_read: Identify what a finished industrial system adds beyond the computing module.
readings.why_this_reading: This catches missing power, protection, interfaces, enclosure and qualification work in a board-only comparison.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A completeness check for the proposed test configurations.

questions: What exact workload and required service level is the customer buying?
Which requirements are pass/fail constraints before performance or price is compared?
Have you included the same carrier, storage, power, cooling, interfaces, software and support boundary for every candidate?
Which advertised hardware features are actually supported by the software configuration you would test?
Which measurements must run continuously under the intended load and temperature rather than briefly on a bench?
What engineering, qualification and fleet-maintenance tasks differ across candidates?
Are quoted prices comparable in date, currency, quantity, taxes and production versus evaluation status?
Which alternative did you omit, and what application-specific reason justifies that omission?
evidence_required: A one-page workload specification with pass/fail requirements.
A full-system bill-of-components and support matrix for each candidate.
A user-run test protocol with software version, load, temperature, power and repeatability recorded.

public: Official specifications, revision ledgers, lifecycle policies and software support documents.
terminal: Use licensed industry research to expand the candidate universe and retrieve independent benchmark methodology; do not equate a market-share table with suitability for this job.
human: Ask an engineer who has shipped products on at least two platforms to critique the workload and test boundaries.
Run the same workload on borrowed or lab hardware if available; record setup and maintenance effort as well as performance.
Ask purchasing for a hypothetical comparable-volume quote through a normal disclosed inquiry if you later choose to contact vendors.

dossiers.completion_test: Hand the comparison protocol to another engineer and have them reproduce the configurations. Explain which requirements each source establishes and which can only be resolved by testing or a customer decision; leave the final ranking to your own work.

dossiers.title: End markets, customer geography and the route to market
dossiers.focus: Learn how the company defines markets and customers, then reconcile geographic and market-share statements before using them in a pitch.

definitions.definition: The company separates Industrial and Embedded from Enthusiast and Education in its operating discussion. The denominator and year of any percentage still need to be checked.
The annual revenue note allocates geography by customer location; that is not automatically the final destination or use of the product.
The prospectus combines third-party research and company assumptions; preserve the category, measurement year and units of each input.

readings.title: Read the historical market definitions
readings.what_to_read: Record the definitions, years and denominators behind market mix and market-share statements.
readings.why_this_reading: Percentages from different populations cannot be compared simply because they are on adjacent pages.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A claim dictionary with numerator, denominator, year, geography and attribution.

readings.title: Read the addressable-market construction
readings.what_to_read: Follow the source dates and assumptions for E&E and semiconductor addressable markets.
readings.why_this_reading: These estimates describe different product universes and are not all directly served revenue pools.
readings.evidence_to_capture: An input tree that identifies researched inputs, company assumptions and resulting categories.

readings.title: Read the historic route and regional requirements
readings.what_to_read: Read regional certification rollout, sales presence and customer support.
readings.why_this_reading: A shipment destination is only part of the work required to enter and serve a market.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A market-entry responsibility list: approvals, channel, applications support and logistics.

readings.title: Read the current customer segmentation
readings.what_to_read: Separate large OEM, mid-sized OEM, smaller/start-up and enthusiast/education routes; inspect the definition behind the mix headline.
readings.why_this_reading: The latest segmentation uses its own commercial and metric boundaries.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A current segment/channel/support matrix with the exact metric basis beside each share.

readings.title: Read the global-footprint claims
readings.what_to_read: Read the outside-UK headline, locations, reseller count and trade-show discussion.
readings.why_this_reading: A public activity count is not proof of commercial conversion.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A list of geographic claims and the measurement basis that still requires clarification.

readings.title: Reconcile the accounting geography
readings.what_to_read: Read the geography table, customer-location basis and major-customer note.
readings.why_this_reading: This is the controlled financial disclosure to compare with the narrative geography statement.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A two-column comparison of customer billing location and claimed end-market geography; do not force a reconciliation with invented data.

readings.title: Read conversion stages and local support
readings.what_to_read: Read who supports inquiries and what makes a discussion become engineering work.
readings.why_this_reading: A geographic expansion question becomes more concrete when roles and stages are identified.
readings.evidence_to_capture: A regional interview plan organized by role and completed customer process.

questions: What is included in each market label, and does the percentage measure revenue, board units or a broader market?
Which inputs to the addressable-market figures are third-party estimates and which are company assumptions?
Can the outside-UK narrative figure and customer-location revenue table be reconciled from public disclosure?
Where are the buyer, reseller, product designer, assembler and final user located in the customer example?
Which approvals, support or logistics requirements change when entering a new region?
What do reseller count, trade-show attendance and project discussion count actually measure?
What evidence connects a new regional relationship to qualification and recurring production purchases?
Which market figures need a terminal refresh and which need a definition from IR before any refresh would be meaningful?
evidence_required: A market-claim dictionary with years and denominators.
An addressable-market input tree without a new market-size estimate.
A customer-versus-end-use geography reconciliation and unresolved-definition list.

public: Prospectus market definitions and footnotes; annual route-to-market and revenue note; regional product approvals.

protocol.action: Record source dates and versions from the issue, PR and release; distinguish authored, merged and released dates.

protocol.action: Read the issue’s exact symptom and environment and the narrower PR change. Keep file listing behaviour and typed-path acceptance distinct.
